episode_title: Ep 131 - The right way to use AI in B2B Sales Alex Boyd & George Coudounaris

real_qa.q: What are the core sales fundamentals that Alex Boyd applies consistently across different go-to-market shifts and companies?
real_qa.r: Alex learned need, feature, benefit training early in his career at a trading brokerage, reinforced by trainers sitting next to him. He realized the fundamental approach is to sit down and help someone get comfortable with a product rather than running a manipulative sales process. He applies this by asking himself: if I were a consultant paid by the hour to help this person, what would I do and say? This simple framework of listening actively, identifying needs, showing relevant features, and explaining benefits has remained his core sales approach across all his companies for over a decade.

real_qa.q: How does Alex Boyd use AI and technology to improve customer conversations without spamming in B2B sales?
real_qa.r: Alex demonstrates using GitHub tickets and coding agents during live calls to address feature requests. When a prospect mentions missing functionality, he opens GitHub on a screen share, puts in the feature request in real time, tags his agent to build a version, and commits to reviewing it and sending a screenshot by the next day. He frames this as: I will email you a screenshot of it, hopefully I can get this done later today or tomorrow and I'll be ready for you by the time you're ready to sign up. This approach makes prospects excited because it shows he listens and acts on qualified buyer needs rather than scaling bad outbound practices.
real_qa.requete: Alex Boyd AI customer conversations GitHub

real_qa.q: Why does asking what customers love about their current vendor work better than asking what they dislike, according to Alex Boyd?
real_qa.r: When Alex asks what people love about their current social media management tool, they volunteer three paragraphs of positive feedback. When he then asks what they would change, they naturally volunteer dislikes in the same breath. By leading with what do you love about it, the tone of conversation shifts completely because prospects no longer feel like they are being socially engineered by a sales person, and they willingly provide the negative feedback without defensive barriers.
real_qa.requete: what do you love about current vendor sales question

real_qa.q: How should sales professionals ask about contract renewal dates to actually get the information from prospects?
real_qa.r: The approach matters more than the question itself. Alex demonstrates opening with trust-building context: Hey, no pressure at all, I think we have a really compelling opportunity for you given that we work with some peer companies. I don't mean to suggest anything drastic, but based on my conversations with you and other folks in your department, would it be okay if I asked when your renewal date is so I know when it's relevant to bring up some things you may want to consider? This approach gets prospects to voluntarily share renewal dates because it builds permission and context first, whereas leading with aggression like rip out your current vendor and put mine in triggers defensive responses.
real_qa.requete: how to ask renewal date sales call

real_qa.q: What is the difference in sales effectiveness between SDRs measured on meetings booked versus salespeople compensated on closed revenue?
real_qa.r: Sales development representatives focused on opening meeting metrics never develop the skills to qualify whether a prospect actually has a real need or decision timeline, resulting in pipelines that go nowhere. Conversely, bootstrappers and salespeople compensated on closed deals and long-term retention must see the entire buying cycle through and live with the consequences of their approach for years. This incentive structure forces them to develop fundamentals like listening, trust-building, and timing, while SDR-only metrics encourage social engineering openers that prospects have become wise to, creating ineffective outbound programs.
real_qa.requete: SDR meetings booked vs sales commission closed deals
